title: Runtime Artifact Provenance and Service Allowlist
author: Maya Thompson
content:
Overview:

This guide defines the runtime artifact provenance model and the operator-maintained service allowlist required for Redwood on-prem packaging. It standardizes:

- artifact metadata (what we record),
- cryptographic signing and attestation processes (how we prove authenticity),
- local verification playbooks (how operators validate before deploy), and
- the service allowlist lifecycle (how services are authorized to run in customer air-gapped or VPC-managed runtimes).

Intended audience:

- Field operators performing image bake and install
- Release engineers responsible for packaging and attestation
- Security reviewers and compliance teams validating supply-chain evidence

Scope:

Applies to all on-prem runtime artifacts distributed as part of Redwood Private (control plane agents, runtime images, model bundles, pinned kernels, and local operator tooling). Does NOT cover third-party OS updates (see customer node OS patch policy).

Definitions:

- artifact: any binary, container image, or model bundle that will be installed on customer runtime nodes.
- provenance: metadata that links an artifact back to a build, signer, and verification snapshot.
- attestation: signed statement (and optional predicate) asserting an artifact's properties (build ID, SBOM reference, approved model hash).
- allowlist: curated list of service identifiers (binary SHA256 or container image digest) permitted to execute within the runtime sandbox.

Principles:

1) Minimal trusted surface: provenance must identify the build pipeline and an authorized signer.
2) Deterministic verification: verification steps are automated and repeatable by field operators.
3) Forensic-friendly: telemetry and retention policies preserve enough signals to reconstruct an install timeline for 90 days.

Provenance metadata schema (human-readable table):

- name: Artifact filename or image tag
- kind: container | binary | model-bundle
- build_id: CI pipeline run id (e.g. rwd-ci/2026-1023)
- digest: sha256:... (container/image digest or artifact SHA256)
- signer: principal who signed (service account or HSM key id)
- signature: base64 signature reference or external attestation link
- sbom_ref: link to SBOM (cyclonedx/spdx) stored in evidence bucket
- build_time_utc: 2026-01-12T15:23:00Z
- provenance_version: v1 (this document)
- approved_for: list of release channels (onprem-stable, onprem-candidate)
- allowed_services: list of service IDs for initial allowlist population

Example provenance manifest (YAML snippet):

---
name: rwd-runtime-agent-1.9.2.tar.gz
kind: binary
build_id: rwd-ci/2026-01234
digest: sha256:8d1f3a...
signer: ksm://hsm-prod/keys/rwd-release-2026
signature: s3://rwd-evidence/attestations/rwd-runtime-agent-1.9.2.sig
sbom_ref: s3://rwd-evidence/sboms/rwd-runtime-agent-1.9.2.cdx.json
build_time_utc: 2026-01-10T21:08:00Z
provenance_version: v1
approved_for: [onprem-stable]
allowed_services: [rwd-agent, rwd-qos-proxy]
---

Signing and attestation flow (operator-facing):

1) Build pipeline produces artifact and SBOM and records build_id.
2) CI uploads artifact and SBOM to internal artifact registry and registers a provisional provenance manifest.
3) Release engineer triggers attestation: signing key managed in HSM (key id format ksm://hsm-prod/keys/...). Use cosign-compatible workflow; tooling wraps HSM signing.
4) Attestation is pushed to evidence storage (S3/GCS or customer-staged object store) and provenance manifest is updated with signature ref.

Commands (example, adapt per-field tooling):

# verify digest and signature locally
$ rwd-verify --artifact rwd-runtime-agent-1.9.2.tar.gz --manifest provenance.yaml
expected output: OK: signature verified by ksm://hsm-prod/keys/rwd-release-2026

# fetch SBOM and quick-check for unexpected packages
$ curl -fsS $(jq -r .sbom_ref provenance.yaml) | jq '.components[] | select(.license==null)'

Local verification playbook (pre-install checklist):

1) Confirm manifest provenance_version == v1.
2) Confirm digest matches artifact on disk: sha256sum <file> == digest in manifest.
3) Validate signature against authorized signer key id. Reject if signer not in authorized_signers list.
4) Fetch SBOM and quick audit for banned packages or unexpected runtimes.
5) Validate allowed_services entries map to services in deployment manifest.
6) Record verification result to local operator journal and push minimal telemetry envelope (verification success/failure, build_id, digest) to evidence collector (see telemetry section).

Service allowlist lifecycle:

- Initial population: During package creation, product leads propose allowed_services; security reviews and field testing gate inclusion.
- Approval: Change proposal goes through release-candidate signoff and is recorded in the allowlist ledger (signed change log stored alongside provenance).
- Operator application: Operators deploy allowlist to the tenant's policy service before first runtime start. The runtime enforces execution by digest comparison.
- Emergency exemption: Operators may temporarily permit a service via a signed operator-exemption token (time-limited, max 4 hours) and must file a post-mortem within 48 hours.

Allowlist format (line-based):

# service-id | kind | digest | reason | approved_by | approved_at
rwd-agent|binary|sha256:8d1f3a...|initial deploy|release-engineering@redwood.com|2026-01-12T22:00:00Z

Enforcement model (runtime):

- At exec-time the runtime resolver: computes artifact digest -> checks allowlist -> verifies signature cache.
- If either check fails, the runtime denies exec and emits a denial reason to local audit socket.
- A degraded mode exists where the runtime runs minimal quarantined process with network disabled for debugging; this mode requires operator manual approval and records full forensic telemetry.

Telemetry and retention (forensics-aware):

- Minimum telemetry emitted on verification: build_id, digest, signer_id, verification_result (pass|fail), timestamp, operator_id (if manual).
- Retention window for full verification envelopes: 90 days (default).
- Anonymized digest index (sha256 prefixes) retained 365 days for cross-tenant threat hunting (where customer consented).
- Evidence storage policy: SBOMs and attestations are immutable and versioned for 3 years (to support compliance audits).

Upgrade and rollback interactions:

- Upgrades must pass provenance verification against the target allowlist entry before swap.
- Rollbacks re-apply previously-approved allowlist values and must re-run provenance verification for the rollback artifact (digest and signature).
- If rollback artifact provenance is missing, operators must:
  1) halt automated rollback,
  2) escalate to release team, and
  3) only permit manual rollback with signed operator exemption + recorded justification.

Operator runbook (quick steps):

1) Preflight: rwd-verify --artifact <file> --manifest provenance.yaml
2) Apply allowlist: rwd-allowlist apply --file allowlist.txt --env tenant-1234
3) Start runtime: rwd-runtimectl start --env tenant-1234
4) Validate runtime acceptance: rwd-runtimectl status --env tenant-1234 | grep -E "allowlist|verification"
5) If verification fails, collect traces: rwd-collect-trace --selector verification_failure --out /tmp/forensic-<ts>.tgz and open an object in the evidence bucket.

SLOs and operational thresholds:

- Verification latency: median 1.5s, p95 5s for local verification against cached signer keys.
- Evidence upload: attestation upload must complete within 60s of signing step in CI.
- Operator manual-exemption window: max 4 hours; approval recorded and telemetry emitted immediately.

Appendix A — Example audit evidence entry (JSON envelope, single-line):

{"timestamp":"2026-01-12T22:01:05Z","build_id":"rwd-ci/2026-01234","artifact":"rwd-runtime-agent-1.9.2.tar.gz","digest":"sha256:8d1f3a...","signer":"ksm://hsm-prod/keys/rwd-release-2026","verification_result":"pass","operator":"auto-ci"}

Appendix B — Troubleshooting matrix (common failures):

- signature mismatch: verify HSM key mapping and that artifact digest was not truncated in transit.
- sbom missing: block install; request SBOM from release owner and attach as urgent evidence.
- allowlist absent: reject install; check allowlist ledger for pending approvals.
